meta.name: US Staffing Payroll Compliance Dataset
meta.disclaimer: Reference information compiled from official government sources. Not legal or tax advice. Check the cited source before relying on any value.

facts.value: immediately at the time of termination (including accrued vacation)
facts.summary: California: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due immediately at the time of termination (including accrued vacation).
facts.evidence_quote: An employee who is discharged must be paid all of his or her wages, including accrued vacation, immediately at the time of termination. Labor Code Sections 201 and 227.3
facts.source_title: Paydays, pay periods, and the final wages (California DIR, Labor Commissioner's Office)
facts.source_publisher: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Labor Standards Enforcement
facts.notes: Industry exceptions exist (seasonal food processing, motion pictures, oil drilling, venue hiring halls) per the same page.

facts.value: at the time of quitting if 72 hours notice was given; otherwise within 72 hours of quitting
facts.summary: California: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due at the time of quitting if 72 hours notice was given; otherwise within 72 hours of quitting.
facts.evidence_quote: An employee without a written employment contract for a definite period of time who quits without giving 72 hours prior notice must be paid all of his or her wages, including accrued vacation, within 72 hours of quitting. Labor Code Section 202
facts.source_title: Paydays, pay periods, and the final wages (California DIR, Labor Commissioner's Office)
facts.source_publisher: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Labor Standards Enforcement
facts.notes: With at least 72 hours prior notice, wages are due at the time of quitting (Labor Code 202, same page).

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: California basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $16.90.
facts.evidence_quote: Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $16.90 Any work in excess of eight hours in one workday, in excess of 40 hours in one workweek, or in the first eight hours worked on the seventh day of work in any one workweek shall be at the rate of one and one-half times the regular rate of pay. Any work in excess of 12 hours in one day or in excess of eight hours on any seventh day of a workweek shall be paid no less than twice the regular rate of pay. California Labor Code section 510. Exceptions apply to an employee working pursuant to an alternative workweek adopted pursuant to applicable Labor Code secti
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.

facts.value: Yes. The independent contractor information must be reported within twenty (20) calendar days of either making payments totaling $600 or more, or entering into a contract for $600 or more with an independent contractor in any calendar year, whichever is earlier.
facts.summary: California independent contractor reporting required? (per OCSE): Yes. The independent contractor information must be reported within twenty (20) calendar days of either making payments totaling $600 or more, or entering into a contract for $600 or more with an independent contractor in any calendar year, whichever is earlier.
facts.evidence_quote: Independent Contractor Reporting Required?: Yes. The independent contractor information must be reported within twenty (20) calendar days of either making payments totaling $600 or more, or entering into a contract for $600 or more with an independent contractor in any calendar year, whichever is earlier.
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: California new hire reporting timeframe (per OCSE): Within 20 days of hire date
facts.evidence_quote: Reporting Timeframe: Within 20 days of hire date
facts.source_title: State New Hire Reporting, State Contact and Program Information (HHS OCSE Intergovernmental Reference Guide)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Child Support Services
facts.notes: Federal floor is 20 days; states may set shorter deadlines. Text as entered by the state in the OCSE guide.

facts.summary: California: frequencies marked in the U.S. DOL State Payday Requirements table: Weekly (note 10); Bi-weekly (note 10); Semi-monthly; Monthly.
facts.source_title: State Payday Requirements (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Note 10: California and Michigan. The frequency of payday depends on the occupation. | DOL table last revised 2023-01-01; DOL says to consult the state labor office for official information. Confirm against current state law before relying on it.

facts.value: Most wages at least twice per calendar month on designated regular paydays
facts.summary: California pay frequency rule: Most wages at least twice per calendar month on designated regular paydays.
facts.evidence_quote: In California, wages, with some exceptions (see table below), must be paid at least twice during each calendar month on the days designated in advance as regular paydays.
facts.source_title: Paydays, pay periods, and the final wages (California DIR)
facts.source_publisher: California Department of Industrial Relations, Division of Labor Standards Enforcement

facts.summary: California employers have a 1.5% FUTA credit reduction for 2026, so the effective FUTA rate is 2.1% on the first $7,000 per employee (if the full state credit applies).
facts.source_title: Final 2026 Federal Unemployment Tax Act (FUTA) Credit Reductions (updated November 10, 2026)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration

facts.summary: California base new employer UI rate: 3.40%.
facts.evidence_quote: New employers are assigned a 3.4 percent UI rate for two to three years.
facts.source_title: Contribution Rates, Withholding Schedules, and Meals and Lodging Values (CA EDD)
facts.notes: Rate basis: UI only. Employers also pay ETT of 0.1% on the same $7,000 wage base (3.5% total, see CA.ui.total_new_employer_rate). Employees pay SDI of 1.3% in 2026 with no wage cap (employee-paid, not an employer cost). UI range 1.5% to 6.2% (Schedule F+).

facts.summary: California experience-rated UI tax rates range from 1.50% to 6.20%.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance
facts.notes: DOL footnote 3: min/max rates apply only to experience-rated employers and exclude surtaxes, surcharges and non-UI taxes. Footnote 4: new employer rate shown is the base rate; higher rates may apply by industry or other factors. DOL notes the report is not an official interpretation of state law.

facts.summary: California state unemployment taxable wage base: $7,000 per employee.
facts.source_title: Significant Provisions of State Unemployment Insurance Laws, Effective July 2026
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Employment and Training Administration, Office of Unemployment Insurance

facts.summary: California 2026 total new employer rate: 3.5% (3.4% UI + 0.1% ETT, both on the first $7,000).
facts.evidence_quote: New employers are assigned a 3.4 percent UI rate for two to three years. ... The ETT rate for 2026 is 0.1 percent. The ETT taxable wage limit is $7,000 per employee, per calendar year.
facts.source_title: Contribution Rates, Withholding Schedules, and Meals and Lodging Values (CA EDD)
facts.notes: Sum of two published rates on the same $7,000 wage base. Employee SDI (1.3%) is not an employer cost.
